title: Financial Assistance Relief Percent on Member Appeals to Out-of-Network Plans Paying First (Insurance Coverage & Claims)
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims — member appeals to an out-of-network plan that pays first.** Questions on how an award under the **Patient Financial Assistance Program** enters the member's contested exposure, which is the exposed charges less the member's leftover, times one hundred less the relief percent, divided by one hundred.

**What is the relief percent?**
The first-plan member appeal's relief percent is the discount percent of the patient's approved financial-assistance award where that award's window, from its start date through its end date, covers the order's collection date and the award's tier carries a discount percent above zero; it is the first-plan hardship percent of **50** where such a covering award carries a discount percent of zero; otherwise it is zero.

**Which award is read?**
The patient's award whose status is approved, with its start date, end date and the discount percent of its tier.

**Which date must the window cover?**
The collection date of the order the appealed claim bills. The window includes its start date and its end date.

**Hypothetical: award at a 25 percent discount, window covering the collection date.** Relief percent 25. Exposed charges of 255.00 USD less a leftover of 102.00 USD leave 153.00 USD; times 75, divided by one hundred, the contested exposure is 114.75 USD.

**Hypothetical: covering award whose tier carries a discount percent of zero.** Relief percent 50.

**Hypothetical: approved award whose window ended before the collection date, or no approved award.** Relief percent zero.
